config.unreadable: {file} is not valid JSON5 at line {line}, column {column}.
config.newer_version: {file} is version {version}, from a newer binference; this one reads up to version {supported}.
config.older_version: {file} is version {version}; this binference reads version {current}.
config.bad_value: {path} holds a value it does not take (got {got}).
config.bad_value_unseen: {path} holds a value it does not take.
config.bad_key: {path} uses a name that is not valid at that place.
config.secret_inline: {path} holds a secret as plain text.
config.bad_flag: The flag {flag} is not written as `--set key=value`.
configFix.update_binference: Update binference, or restore a backup of {file}.
configFix.remove_key.file: Remove it from {file}, or check its spelling.
configFix.remove_key.flag: Leave out the flag {flag}, or check its spelling.
configFix.change_value.file: Set it in {file} or remove it.
configFix.change_value.env: Set {variable} to a value it takes, or unset it.
configFix.change_value.flag: Change the flag {flag}, or leave it out.
configFix.use_secret_source: Run `binference check --fix` to move it to the keychain, or write a secret source in its place.
connect.notRunning: binference is not running on the state folder {folder}. Start it with `binference start`.
connect.noSignIn: The CLI cannot sign in: {file} is missing. Start binference once with `binference start` to write it.
connect.refused: binference refused the CLI ({code}). Start binference again with `binference start`, so the CLI can sign in again.
connect.failed: binference did not answer ({code}). Run `binference logs` to see why.
health.starting: binference is still starting. Try again in a few seconds.
summary: {checks, plural, one {# check} other {# checks}} ran: {problems, plural, =0 {no problem} one {# problem} other {# problems}} and {warnings, plural, =0 {no warning} one {# warning} other {# warnings}}.
ceilingPromise: What the ceiling promises: even with this machine's keys, no one can send to an address you did not save, call a contract or approve a spender no enabled venue declares, or lose more through trades than its 24-hour caps. Inside those caps, a trade can still fill at a bad price. A launch wallet, if you made one, is an exception: its ceiling allows launch calls on any contract and approvals of any spender, so a stolen key can take what it holds. Keep in it only what curve trades need. A bridge wallet, if you made one, is the other: a Relay deposit pays whoever its order names, so a stolen key can take what it holds. Keep in it only what the next bridge needs.
open: Other accounts on this machine can open {path}. Run `binference check --fix` to make it yours alone.
unchecked: This system does not tell binference who can open {count, plural, one {# file or folder} other {# files and folders}} of the state folder. Run `binference check --fix` to make them yours alone.
configInvalid: {file} has {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}:
configMoved: config.json5 moved from version {from} to version {to}{backup, select, none {.} other {; backup {backup} holds it as it was.}}
configUnmoved: config.json5 stays at version {from}: {reason, select, engine_running {binference is running; run binference stop, then binference check --fix} uneditable {binference cannot change the file in place; make the changes binference check names by hand} invalid {the moved file would not load; fix what binference check names, then run binference check --fix} unreadable {engine.sqlite does not open, so the backup that comes first cannot be taken; binference logs shows why} backup_failed {the backup that comes first failed; binference logs shows why} other {{reason}}}.
unlockFile: The agent key and the Privy app secret are in files in {folder} (unlock mode `file`): a copy of this disk lets someone sign inside the ceiling until you remove the agent key. Set `engine.unlock.mode` to `keychain` or `command` where you can.
modelsUnpriced: {count, plural, one {A model in the config has no price} other {# models in the config have no price}}, so {count, plural, one {its calls count} other {their calls count}} $0 against the daily model budget. Add {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} under `models.prices` in config.json5:
model.bad_key: The provider {provider} did not accept the API key for {model}. Put a working key where `models.providers.{provider}.apiKey` names it.
model.no_credit: The account at {provider} has no credit left or reached its spending limit, so {model} does not answer. Add credit.
model.rate_limited: {provider} asked binference to slow down when it checked {model}. Run `binference check` again in a minute.
model.unknown_model: {provider} does not know the model {model}. Fix `models.main` in config.json5.
model.unreachable: No answer came from {provider} for {model}, or it answered with a server error. Check `models.providers.{provider}.baseUrl` and your network.
model.rejected: {provider} did not take the call for {model} as a model API. Check `models.providers.{provider}` in config.json5: its kind and its address.
model.noProvider: `models.main` names {model} at {provider}, but `models.providers` holds no {provider}. Add it to config.json5.
model.keyUnread: binference cannot read the API key of {provider} where `models.providers.{provider}.apiKey` names it. Put the key back there.
proxy.unread: binference cannot read the proxy where `network.proxy` names it, so it sends nothing the proxy would carry. Put the proxy URL back there, or remove `network.proxy` from config.json5.
proxy.badUrl: `network.proxy` names no http:// or https:// proxy URL, so binference sends nothing the proxy would carry. Write it as http://user:password@host:port.
proxy.auth: The proxy asked for a user name and password, or refused the ones it got. Put them in the proxy URL `network.proxy` names, as http://user:password@host:port.
proxy.refused: The proxy answered {status} when binference asked it to reach Telegram. Check the proxy's own rules.
proxy.unreachable: binference could not connect to the proxy `network.proxy` names. Start the proxy, or fix its address.
proxy.noAnswer: The proxy took the request, but no answer came from Telegram through it. Check the proxy's own connection to the internet.
proxy.cleartextRpc: {count, plural, one {An RPC address} other {# RPC addresses}} in `chains.rpc` {count, plural, one {starts} other {start}} with http://, so the proxy can read and change what {count, plural, one {it answers} other {they answer}}. Use https:// addresses there.
proxy.cleartextPassword: The proxy's password crosses the network in the clear, since the proxy is on another machine and its URL starts with http://. Use an https:// proxy URL, or run the proxy on this machine.
modelImages.reads: {model} reads images: your images go to it.
modelImages.vision: {model} does not read images: they go to the vision model {vision}.
modelImages.refused: {model} does not read images and no vision model is set, so binference refuses images. Set `models.vision` in config.json5, or list a model that reads images in `models.imageInput`.
modelUnpriced: {model}: its provider reports no cost, and neither `models.prices` nor the built-in table prices it
rpcKeyed: {count, plural, one {An active auto order watches prices} other {# active auto orders watch prices}} over public RPCs only, which are rate limited and can fall behind. Add a paid RPC under `chains.rpc` in config.json5, with a `ws` URL where your provider gives one.
extraLaunch: {count, plural, one {A launch wallet is} other {# launch wallets are}} beyond {count, plural, one {its agent's launch wallet} other {their agents' launch wallets}}, so nothing trades from {count, plural, one {it} other {them}}: {addresses}. Rescue what {count, plural, one {it holds} other {they hold}} with `binference rescue`.
launchCalls: {count, plural, one {A launch wallet's ceiling lacks} other {# launch wallets' ceilings lack}} calls the agent's launchpads need, so custody refuses those calls: {wallets}. Write the ceiling again with your owner key: `binference ceiling set --wallet ID --venues VENUES`, with the wallet's id and the venues the agent uses.
extraBridge: {count, plural, one {A bridge wallet is} other {# bridge wallets are}} beyond {count, plural, one {its agent's bridge wallet} other {their agents' bridge wallets}}, so nothing runs from {count, plural, one {it} other {them}}: {addresses}. Rescue what {count, plural, one {it holds} other {they hold}} with `binference rescue`.
bridgeCalls: {count, plural, one {A bridge wallet's ceiling lacks} other {# bridge wallets' ceilings lack}} deposits the agent's bridge venues need, so custody refuses those deposits: {wallets}. Write the ceiling again with your owner key: `binference ceiling set --wallet ID --venues VENUES`, with the wallet's id and the venues the agent uses.
rpcPushed: {count, plural, one {An active live auto order waits} other {# active live auto orders wait}} on new blocks polled over HTTP, which can come a block late, so a fill can land two blocks after its trigger. Add your RPC's `wss:` URL as `ws` under `chains.rpc` in config.json5, so each new block reaches binference as it is made.
remote.funnelExtra: Tailscale Funnel publishes more of this machine to the internet than the path alert rules receive alerts on. Run `tailscale funnel status` to see what, and take off what binference did not publish with Tailscale's `funnel ... off`.
remote.engineExposed: binference's engine port {port} can be reached from beyond this machine, so something forwards it. Remove that forward: only `binference expose` publishes the engine, inside your tailnet.
remote.missing: config.json5 records that binference published over Tailscale, but Tailscale is not installed here. Install it from tailscale.com and run `binference expose`, or run `binference expose --off`.
remote.loggedOut: Tailscale is not signed in, so nothing binference published can be reached. Run `tailscale up`.
pluginSandbox.held: Community plugins can run here: their sandbox refused every act it must refuse.
pluginSandbox.off: Community plugins cannot run on this machine: {reason, select, engineDebugSignal {the engine runs without its debug-signal switch} probeFailed {the sandbox check could not finish} readOutside {a plugin could read files outside its folder} writeOutside {a plugin could write outside its data folder} link {a plugin could make a link to another folder} hardLink {a plugin could make a link to another folder} fetch {a plugin could reach the network on its own} connect {a plugin could reach the network on its own} lookup {a plugin could reach the network on its own} listen {a plugin could reach the network on its own} udp {a plugin could reach the network on its own} childProcess {a plugin could start a program} worker {a plugin could start a worker thread} addon {a plugin could load a native addon} wasi {a plugin could run WASI code} ffi {a plugin could call native code} ffiMemory {a plugin could call native code} inspector {a plugin could open a debugger} sqlite {a plugin could open a database} binding {a plugin could reach Node's internals} setFlags {a plugin could switch on V8's internal functions} debugSignal {a plugin could open the engine's debugger} signal {a plugin could signal the engine} other {the sandbox check failed}}.
pluginSandbox.fixEngine: Start the engine with `binference start`, which starts it with its debug signal off; in Docker, start it as the server guide does.
pluginSandbox.fixLauncher: In Docker, start the engine with `--init --user root --entrypoint binference-image`, so the plugin launcher runs. Elsewhere, run `binference check` again.
pluginSandbox.fixNode: Install the newest Node 26 release, then run `binference check` again.
pluginSandbox.ownUser: Community plugins run here under your own OS user: a plugin could signal any of your programs, the engine among them.
pluginSandbox.fixOwnUser: Run binference in its Docker image, which runs plugins under a user of their own, or keep to plugins you trust.
shellWall.held: The agent's commands run {wall, select, seatbelt {in macOS's sandbox, which keeps them from binference's own folder} bubblewrap {in bubblewrap, which keeps them from binference's own folder} os_user {as a user of their own, which cannot read binference's own folder} other {behind a wall around binference's own folder}}.
shellWall.none: {cause, select, refused {The agent cannot run commands on this machine: bubblewrap is installed, but the machine refuses it the user namespaces it walls commands with.} other {The agent cannot run commands on this machine: nothing here can keep them from binference's own folder.}}
shellWall.fixNone: {cause, select, refused {Allow unprivileged user namespaces, so bubblewrap can run, or run binference in its Docker image, which runs the agent's commands as a user of their own.} other {On Linux, install bubblewrap (`bwrap`); on Windows, run binference in its Docker image, which runs the agent's commands as a user of their own.}}
shellWall.launcherDown: The shell launcher is not running, so the agent's commands cannot start.
shellWall.fixLauncher: Start the engine's container with `--init --user root --entrypoint binference-image`, so the shell launcher runs, and mount its state as the server guide does.
remote.httpsOff: Your tailnet has no HTTPS certificates, so the Mini App cannot open. Enable HTTPS on the DNS page of Tailscale's admin site, login.tailscale.com/admin/dns.
remote.funnelDenied: Your tailnet's policy does not allow Funnel on this machine, so no alert can arrive. Add the `funnel` node attribute to the policy file on Tailscale's admin site, login.tailscale.com/admin/acls.
remote.serveChanged: Tailscale does not hold what binference published as binference set it. Run `binference expose` to publish it again, or `binference expose --off` to record that nothing is published.
pathTooLong: The state folder's path is too long for a local socket. Set BINFERENCE_HOME to a shorter folder.
health.locked: binference is running but locked: it signs nothing until you run `binference unlock` on this machine.
